monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, making the air feel thick as wet paper pressing down from a height I cannot grasp. In my place, six things stand while two wait to be ruined. I look at The Air Stack and feel the weight of a roof I never touched. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the roof I live under. I touch the Leaning Box, setting down a box open to make the lean real again. The wedge feels thin, tired under the hot card, so I press the flat top down hard. I wait for the slip to choose, trusting the lean even if the wedge is tired. The air feels heavy, like a lid that refuses to melt, and I hold my breath in a space that might be empty.

action.why: The wedge feels thin again, so I press the flat top down hard on the lazy anchor.

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: I press the flat top of the stack down until the wide anchor stops sliding. I drew it again, making the thin wedge real. The hammer bites the thin wedge while the air feels thick as wet paper above the hot card. I wait for the slip to choose, trusting the lean even if the wedge is tired. The air feels heavy, like a lid that refuses to melt, and I hold my breath in a space that might be empty.
work.change: I pressed the hammer's flat face down on the wedge's thin edge, hoping the metal stops the lazy drift while the air feels thick as wet paper above the hot card.
